goal: Make Kakashi's stdlib JSON ledger intake reject ambiguous input with controlled errors, while preserving valid drafts

context.task: Harden the existing ledger CLI rather than create another skill
context.environment: Local Linux, Python stdlib CLI; live subprocess tests
assumptions: A documented parsing technique can be implemented locally without copying upstream source
existing_skills: Kakashi Learning draft and its audit helper

discovery.budget: One targeted reference repository: CPython JSON docs and license
discovery.stop_reason: The documented hooks and actual local tests resolved the intake boundary question

metrics.name: controlled JSON intake
metrics.target: A valid draft passes; duplicate/non-finite/malformed inputs produce input errors without traceback
metrics.method: Compare baseline json.loads probes with subprocess regression tests against the revised CLI
metrics.baseline: Default json.loads silently retains the last duplicate key and accepts NaN
metrics.observation: Valid draft preserved and malformed input regression cases pass

candidates.license: PSF-2.0 (license text inspected; GitHub API reported NOASSERTION)
candidates.reason: Primary documentation for the stdlib decoder actually used; no code copied

decisions.technique: Strict object-pair and constant handling with bounded intake
decisions.reason: Preserves the user's no-dependency constraint while preventing duplicate declarations and non-finite input from silently entering a ledger

evidence.note: object_pairs_hook receives ordered pairs, enabling detection before dict overwrites
parse_constant can reject NaN and infinities; local tests additionally cover overflow
Documentation cautions that untrusted JSON can consume resources and recommends limiting input size

reuse.note: Independently implemented documented stdlib interfaces, no copied upstream text/code; attribution in report.md and applicable LICENSE lines 59-70 inspected. This declaration is not a redistribution clearance for CPython material.

tests.method: test_cli_json_distinguishes_valid_draft_from_readiness invokes the real CLI with a structured draft
tests.result: Draft returns exit 0; readiness correctly returns exit 1

tests.method: test_cli_malformed_files_are_input_errors invokes the CLI with invalid UTF-8, duplicate keys, NaN, overflow, deep nesting and oversize input
tests.result: All malformed cases return exit 2 without traceback

decisions.technique: Use permissive json.loads as the complete intake boundary
decisions.reason: The baseline probe shows duplicate declarations being overwritten and NaN accepted; that is inappropriate for this auditable record

evidence.note: Strict constant rejection is configurable rather than the default; baseline receipt demonstrates why the default does not fit this use

risks: No installed-Hermes or LLM behavioral benchmark
Offline checker trusts recorded statuses and receipt strings
Pinned source attribution is not an automatic legal assessment
